speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how many companies in the tourism-related and retail sectors have closed down since January 2020; (b) what is the employment situation in the tourism sector including number of tour guides who have been redeployed; and (c) what further efforts can the made to stimulate local retail demand and transform the tourism sector to position themselves for future growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For the tourism industry, despite some exits since January 2020, new entrants have kept the number of tourism businesses in operation fairly stable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, the number of licensed hotels today remains at around 420 despite 13 hotels having ceased operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Travel agents, unfortunately, have been impacted more – 157 travel agents ceased their operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This represent 8% of all licensed travel agents, although around 30 new travel agents entered the market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government has supported the sector with the highest tier of support under the Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Together with other broad-based Government support measures, this has helped cushion the impact of COVID-19 on the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Initiatives such as the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers (SRV) scheme have also helped stimulate demand by encouraging Singaporeans to rediscover our city, our tourism product offerings and support local tourism businesses, including those for travel agents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The launch of the SRV scheme has also helped tourist guides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Between the launch of the SRV scheme and the start of the Heightened Alert in May 2021, monthly tour participants grew fivefold from just over 10,000 to more than 50,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To further help our tourist guides cope with business costs, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) also waived the tourist guide licence fees in 2020 and 2021, as well as test fees for those who wish to be licensed in another language.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: STB expects tourism to reach pre-pandemic levels in the next few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In the meantime, we are helping companies in the retail and tourism sectors transform and upgrade themselves so that they can better capture opportunities when travel resumes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With regard to retailers, for retailers looking to develop their online sales channels, they can receive support from Enterprise Singapore’s (ESG) E-Commerce Booster Package, which defrays the costs of joining e-commerce platforms, or use ESG’s Productivity Solutions Grant to build capabilities in areas such as digital marketing as well as e-commerce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The tourism sector is also receiving support from STB to pursue transformation efforts to ready itself for the recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Examples include the Business Improvement Fund for technology innovation and the adoption of business models and processes to improve productivity and competitiveness; and the Training Industry Professionals in Tourism scheme which supports employee upgrading and talent and leadership development.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is good to hear the Minister of State mentioned that the SRV scheme that has been very useful for the retail and tourism sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But he did share that there were 157 travel agents which have ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My supplementary question is, in particular, about those working in the tourism and retail sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have a number of residents who used to work or are working in the tourism and retail sectors, which have been in partial limbo over the past one and a half years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question is, whether we have the number of tour guides or retail frontline workers who have switched industries or switched jobs permanently.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can I also ask about the status of our local travel agencies in Singapore, and if they will survive, going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Also, what outlook can we expect for the retail sector and the travel agency business in this endemic scenario that we are going to face over the next year or so?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned earlier on in my reply, the SRV scheme has also helped local tourist guides with monthly tour participants growing fivefold between the launch of the SRV scheme and the start of the Heightened Alert in May 2021.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also mentioned earlier on STB waiving the tourist guide licence fees as well as test fees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, all of these in concert, and all of these in totality, are helping preserve our capability in our tourism sector, which is an important sector, while we await the recovery in global travel as well as the tourism industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The SRV, for example, helps us to create new product offerings locally, with tourist guides forming new products.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it will put them in good stead for when travel resumes in earnest, and when tourists come to Singapore and are able to enjoy the sights and sounds here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This translates to 16.9 retrenched employees per 1,000 employees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Of these retrenched employees, 56% were able to enter a different industry within six months after retrenchment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But I also wanted to share a little bit about Enterprise Singapore's Retail Industry Transformation Map (ITM), as a forward-looking roadmap for our retail industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Retail ITM has done a study and they have looked across the key trends in the retail industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The key trends are digitalisation, on-demand retail, hyper-personalisation of goods, in effect, and conscious consumerism, which is very much related to the sustainability trend that we are seeing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we are supporting our retail sector to take on and to ride these trends, moving forward.
